```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.5,
                      out.width = "80%")
```

The check belongs in the design section of a matched study, next to the balance table, and it
is done before any outcome is looked at. This vignette shows how to read the plots and how to
build the Methods and Results text from the result, so that every number and setting comes from
the run.

```{r run}
library(propsens)
data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit", replace = TRUE
)
# The faster model set and small settings so the vignette builds quickly; use the defaults
# (logistic regression, BART and the GRF probability forest) in a real analysis.
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(
  matched, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  seeds = 1:2, n_trees = 100, bootstrap_samples = 5
)
```

## Reading the three plots

**Patients plot** (`plot(x, type = "patients")`). Each point is a treated patient: right = the
kept models place this patient differently among all patients; up = the kept models give this
patient different kinds of untreated partners. The plot describes how the disagreement is spread
over the treated patients; it is a description, and individual points should not be read as
flags for individual patients. Points near the bottom left mean that these models rank the
patient similarly and choose similar partners. Colour shows whether the patient's logistic score
is outside the range of the untreated patients' scores.

**Models plot** (`plot(x, type = "models")`). Each row is a model, each panel a balance
statistic, each axis starting at 0. If the points of a panel line up, the balance you report does
not depend on the model; if they spread out, it does: say so, and show this plot. Filled points
are kept by the quality gate, hollow points are not; your own model has its own colour and is
judged on balance only. The extended-terms panel is usually driven by sparse squares and
interactions; report the main-terms panel.

**Recurrence plot** (`plot(x, type = "recurrence")`). The per-patient pair recurrence behind
pair instability (1 minus its mean over treated patients across the kept models; exploratory).
Values near the floor (1 / number of kept models) are expected when untreated patients are dense,
even when the models agree; report pair instability next to rank disagreement, never alone.

## What to write in Methods

The sentence below is built from the result object: the model set, the gate and how many models
it kept (by algorithm), the matching settings, the share of treated patients kept and the seed.

```{r methods-sentence, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
settings <- sensitivity$settings
models <- sensitivity$models[!sensitivity$models$is_reference, ]
kept <- models[models$in_use, ]
fallback <- sensitivity$quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models
algorithm_names <- c(logistic_regression = "logistic regression",
                     bart = "Bayesian additive regression trees",
                     grf_probability = "a generalized random forest",
                     random_forest = "a random forest", gradient_boosting = "gradient boosting")
fitted_algorithms <- unique(models$algorithm)
fitted_text <- paste(algorithm_names[fitted_algorithms], collapse = ", ")
count_by_algorithm <- table(factor(kept$algorithm, levels = unique(kept$algorithm)))
kept_text <- paste0(as.integer(count_by_algorithm), " ",
                    algorithm_names[names(count_by_algorithm)], collapse = ", ")
smd_words <- "their largest post-match standardized mean difference on main terms"
balance_text <- switch(
  settings$balance_rule,
  relative = sprintf("%s was within %.2f of the best model's and at most %.2f", smd_words,
                     settings$balance_margin, settings$balance_cap),
  relative_only = sprintf("%s was within %.2f of the best model's", smd_words,
                          settings$balance_margin),
  absolute = sprintf("%s was at most %.2f", smd_words, settings$balance_threshold)
)
caliper_text <- if (is.null(settings$caliper_sd)) "" else
  sprintf(" with a caliper of %.2g standard deviations of the logit", settings$caliper_sd)
kept_share <- range(kept$treated_kept)
share_text <- if (all(kept_share >= 1)) "all treated patients were matched" else
  sprintf("%.0f to %.0f %% of treated patients were matched", 100 * kept_share[1],
          100 * kept_share[2])
gate_result <- if (fallback) {
  sprintf(paste("fewer than two of the %d models met these criteria, so all models were",
                "used and the summaries describe all of them"), nrow(models))
} else {
  sprintf("%d of %d models were kept (%s)", nrow(kept), nrow(models), kept_text)
}
cat("> We described the sensitivity of the matched design to the propensity model with the R",
    sprintf("package propsens (version %s).", as.character(utils::packageVersion("propsens"))),
    paste0(toupper(substring(fitted_text, 1, 1)), substring(fitted_text, 2)),
    sprintf("(%d seeds for each tree method; %d models; %d-fold cross-fitted scores; seed %d)",
            length(settings$seeds), nrow(models), settings$folds, settings$seed),
    sprintf("were each used for 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching %s replacement%s.",
            if (settings$replace) "with" else "without", caliper_text),
    sprintf(paste("Models were kept if their cross-fitted log-loss was within %.0f %% of the",
                  "best model's and %s; %s, and %s."),
            100 * settings$quality_tolerance, balance_text, gate_result, share_text),
    "For the kept models we report the mean rank disagreement over treated patients, the",
    "bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model, and the range of the largest",
    "standardized mean difference on main terms. No outcome data were used. These summaries",
    "are descriptive; they have not been validated as predictors of bias.\n")
```

If you reran the check with several values of `seed` (`seed_sensitivity()`), add: "The check
was repeated with seeds 1, 2 and 3; all results are reported."

## What to write in Results

The numbers below come from the run above, not typed by hand:

```{r results-sentence, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
numbers <- sensitivity$summary$table
value <- function(name) numbers$with_gate[numbers$quantity == name]
n_kept <- length(sensitivity$summary$models_used)
ratio <- value("median_between_within_ratio_treated")
ratio_text <- if (is.na(ratio)) "not available (no kept algorithm had two seeds)" else
  sprintf("%.1f", ratio)
results_template <- paste(
  "> Mean rank disagreement over treated patients was %.3f; the bootstrap rank instability of",
  "the logistic model was %.3f. As exploratory summaries, pair instability was %.2f (of a",
  "possible %.2f with %d models) and the median between/within-algorithm ratio was %s. The",
  "largest standardized mean difference on main terms ranged from %.2f to %.2f across the %s."
)
cat(sprintf(results_template, value("mean_rank_disagreement_treated"),
            value("bootstrap_rank_instability_treated"),
            value("pair_instability_models_mean_treated"), 1 - 1 / n_kept, n_kept, ratio_text,
            min(kept$smd_max_main), max(kept$smd_max_main),
            if (fallback) "models" else "kept models"), "\n")
if (sensitivity$kept_algorithms_count == 1 && n_kept >= 2) {
  cat("> The kept models were seeds of a single algorithm, so these summaries describe seed",
      "noise within that algorithm, not disagreement between algorithms.\n")
}
```

If the quality gate left fewer than two models, add: "Fewer than two propensity models met the
quality criteria (log-loss within 5 % of the best model's; largest standardized mean difference
on main terms at most 0.10 above the best model's and at most 0.25), so all models were used."
With `balance_rule = "absolute"`, describe that rule instead; `print()` states the rule in effect.
Call the criteria pre-specified only if you fixed them before running the check.

## If you judge the disagreement to be large

No thresholds exist yet, so this is a judgement you state and justify.

1. Show the models plot (balance by model).
2. Choose the design by balance, never by the outcome.
3. Decide before looking at outcomes whether you will report the effect estimate under each kept
   model, and then report all of them.
4. Look at where the disagreement is concentrated in the patients plot: does it sit in a region
   of the covariates with few untreated patients? Describe this for the study as a whole.

## What the check does not do

It does not detect unmeasured confounding, it does not fix a design, and it does not tell you
which model is right. When logistic regression is correct, the tree models can still disagree
with it: the check describes that the *choice* matters, not which choice is correct. It cannot
tell whether a disagreement matters for the effect estimate, and a small value is not evidence
that the estimate is unbiased. It covers 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching for the ATT only.
